overall: The AG found the Randolph School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by withholding the March 15, 2012 executive session minutes, because its security-deployment purpose still required confidentiality under G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to provide a copy of the March 15, 2012 executive session minutes after a records request.
allegations.key_passage: we are convinced that the Committee's need for confidentiality remains, and that the publication of the March 15, 2012 executive session minutes at this time would defeat the lawful purpose of the executive session

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged no lawful purpose remained to keep the minutes confidential because the security plans had already been made public.
Reviewing the withholding claim, the AG examined whether the March 15, 2012 executive session was held under the security-personnel purpose, Purpose 4.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee met in executive session on March 15, 2012 specifically to discuss "the deployment of security personnel or devices, or strategies with respect thereto" as part of a security plan.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
